recipes.title: Perfect Roast Chicken
recipes.description: Crispy-skinned, juicy roast chicken—the Sunday dinner that defines home cooking.
instructions: Remove chicken from refrigerator 1 hour before cooking.
Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Mix butter with thyme, rosemary, garlic, and half the salt and pepper.
Gently loosen skin over breast and thighs. Spread herb butter under skin.
Season cavity with remaining salt and pepper. Stuff with lemon and onion.
Truss legs together with kitchen twine. Tuck wing tips under.
Rub skin with olive oil and season generously with salt.
Roast 1 hour 15 minutes until thigh reaches 165°F (74°C) and juices run clear.
Rest 15 minutes before carving.
recipes.story: A perfectly roasted chicken is the mark of a good cook. The high-heat method creates crackling skin while the herb butter bastes the meat from within. Sunday dinner at its finest.

recipes.title: Brown Sugar Glazed Ham
recipes.description: A spiral-cut ham with a crackling sweet glaze—the centerpiece of holiday tables.
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C). Place ham cut-side down in a roasting pan.
Cover loosely with foil. Bake 10-12 minutes per pound until internal temp reaches 130°F (54°C).
Meanwhile, mix brown sugar, mustard, honey, orange juice, ground cloves, and cinnamon.
Remove ham from oven. Increase temperature to 425°F (220°C).
Score top of ham in diamond pattern if desired. Stud with whole cloves.
Brush glaze generously over ham.
Return to oven uncovered. Bake 15-20 minutes until glaze is caramelized, brushing twice more.
Let rest 15 minutes before carving.
recipes.story: Glazed ham is the traditional centerpiece for Easter and Christmas dinners. The spiral cut makes carving effortless, and the sweet-savory glaze forms a crackling crust.

recipes.title: Buttermilk Fried Chicken
recipes.description: Perfectly crispy, deeply seasoned fried chicken—the Southern Sunday dinner tradition.
instructions: Combine buttermilk and hot sauce. Submerge chicken and refrigerate 4 hours or overnight.
Mix flour with paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, salt, and pepper.
Remove chicken from buttermilk, shaking off excess.
Dredge thoroughly in seasoned flour. Let rest 15 minutes.
Heat shortening in a cast-iron skillet to 350°F (175°C). Oil should be 1 inch deep.
Fry chicken in batches, turning occasionally. Dark meat: 15-18 minutes. White meat: 12-15 minutes.
Drain on a wire rack. Season with salt while hot.
recipes.story: Fried chicken after church was a weekly ritual in the South. The long buttermilk soak tenderizes the meat and creates an impossibly crunchy crust.

recipes.title: Roast Leg of Lamb
recipes.description: Herb-crusted lamb roasted to pink perfection—the elegant Sunday dinner.
instructions: Remove lamb from refrigerator 2 hours before cooking.
Preheat oven to 450°F (230°C).
Make small slits all over lamb. Insert garlic slices.
Mix rosemary, mint, olive oil, lemon zest, salt, and pepper into a paste.
Rub paste all over lamb.
Place lamb on a rack in a roasting pan.
Roast 20 minutes at 450°F, then reduce to 325°F (165°C).
Continue roasting until internal temp reaches 135°F (57°C) for medium-rare, about 15 minutes per pound.
Rest 20 minutes before carving. Serve with mint jelly.
recipes.source: American Easter and Sunday dinner tradition
recipes.story: Roast lamb is the traditional centerpiece for Easter dinner, but it deserves more frequent appearances. The high-heat start creates a beautiful crust while the lower roast keeps it juicy.

recipes.title: Herb-Crusted Pork Loin Roast
recipes.description: Juicy pork loin with a fragrant herb crust—elegant enough for company, simple enough for family.
instructions: Remove pork from refrigerator 1 hour before cooking.
Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Mix olive oil, garlic, rosemary, sage, thyme, mustard, salt, and pepper into a paste.
Rub paste all over pork, pressing it into the meat.
Place pork on a rack in a roasting pan. Pour cider into pan.
Roast 55-65 minutes until internal temp reaches 145°F (63°C).
Rest 15 minutes—temperature will rise to 150°F (66°C).
Slice and serve with pan juices.
recipes.story: Pork loin is leaner than it used to be, so it needs to be treated carefully. The herb crust adds flavor and helps keep it moist. Don't skip the resting time.

recipes.title: Braised Beef Short Ribs
recipes.description: Deeply caramelized short ribs braised until falling off the bone—the ultimate comfort food.
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C). Season ribs with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a Dutch oven over high heat. Brown ribs on all sides in batches. Remove.
Add onions, carrots, and celery. Cook until caramelized, about 10 minutes.
Add garlic and tomato paste; cook 2 minutes.
Add wine, scraping up browned bits. Simmer until reduced by half.
Add broth, thyme, and bay leaves. Return ribs to pot.
Cover and braise 3 hours until meat is falling off the bone.
Skim fat from sauce. Discard bay leaves and thyme.
Serve ribs with braising liquid and vegetables.
recipes.story: Short ribs were once a budget cut, prized by home cooks who knew that time in a low oven transforms tough meat into silk. The wine-rich braising liquid becomes a luxurious sauce.

recipes.title: Sunday Beef Pot Roast
recipes.description: Falling-apart tender beef braised with root vegetables—the meal that fills the house with warmth.
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C).
Season roast generously with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a Dutch oven over high heat. Sear roast on all sides until well browned. Remove.
Add onions, carrots, and celery. Cook 5 minutes.
Add garlic and tomato paste; cook 1 minute.
Add broth, wine if using, thyme, and bay leaves. Bring to simmer.
Return roast to pot. Cover and braise in oven 2.5 hours.
Add potatoes. Continue braising 1 hour until beef is fork-tender.
Let rest 15 minutes. Slice beef and serve with vegetables and pan juices.
recipes.story: Pot roast went into the oven after church and emerged just as the family gathered. The long braise transforms an economical cut into something extraordinary.

recipes.title: Classic Meat Lasagna
recipes.description: Layers of pasta, rich meat sauce, and three cheeses—the Italian-American Sunday tradition.
instructions: Cook lasagna noodles according to package. Drain and lay flat on oiled sheet.
Brown beef and sausage. Add onion; cook until soft. Add garlic, cook 1 minute.
Stir in tomatoes, tomato paste, Italian seasoning, and salt. Simmer 30 minutes.
Mix ricotta, egg, and parsley.
Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Spread 1 cup meat sauce in a 9x13 pan. Layer: noodles, ricotta mixture, meat sauce, mozzarella, Parmesan.
Repeat layers twice. Top with remaining noodles, sauce, and cheeses.
Cover with foil. Bake 45 minutes. Uncover; bake 15 minutes more.
Rest 15 minutes before cutting.
recipes.story: Lasagna came to represent Italian-American abundance—layers upon layers of goodness. Making it is a labor of love, but it feeds a crowd and gets better the next day.

recipes.title: Perfect Mashed Potatoes
recipes.description: Creamy, buttery, impossibly smooth—the essential side dish done right.
instructions: Place potatoes in a large pot of cold salted water. Bring to boil.
Cook until fork-tender, about 20-25 minutes. Drain well.
Return potatoes to hot pot for 1 minute to dry out excess moisture.
Press potatoes through a ricer or mash thoroughly.
Add butter and stir until melted.
Gradually stir in warm cream and sour cream.
Season with salt and white pepper. Beat until fluffy.
Top with chives if desired. Serve immediately.
recipes.story: The secret to great mashed potatoes: warm your cream, dry your potatoes after draining, and never overwork them or they'll turn gluey. Simple, but technique matters.

recipes.title: Homemade Dinner Rolls
recipes.description: Soft, pillowy rolls fresh from the oven—nothing compares.
instructions: Dissolve yeast in warm milk with a pinch of sugar. Let stand 5 minutes.
Add sugar, melted butter, egg, and salt. Mix well.
Gradually add flour to form a soft dough.
Knead until smooth and elastic, about 8 minutes.
Place in a greased bowl. Cover and let rise 1 hour until doubled.
Punch down. Divide into 24 pieces. Shape into balls.
Place in a greased 9x13 pan, just touching.
Cover and let rise 45 minutes until doubled.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 20-25 minutes until golden.
Brush immediately with melted butter.
recipes.story: Homemade rolls require time, but the aroma of bread baking and the pride of serving something made from scratch makes Sunday dinner special.

recipes.title: Classic Apple Pie
recipes.description: The American dessert—tender spiced apples in a buttery, flaky crust.
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a 9-inch pie plate with bottom crust.
Toss apples with sugars, flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, salt, and lemon juice.
Pile filling into crust, mounding in center. Dot with butter.
Top with second crust. Trim and crimp edges. Cut decorative vents.
Brush with egg wash. Sprinkle with coarse sugar.
Bake 25 minutes at 425°F.
Reduce to 375°F (190°C) and bake 35-40 minutes more until golden and bubbling.
Cool at least 2 hours before slicing.
recipes.story: Apple pie is so American it's cliché—but for good reason. The combination of tart apples, warm spices, and buttery crust is simply perfect. Serve warm with vanilla ice cream.

recipes.title: Classic Chocolate Layer Cake
recipes.description: Rich, moist chocolate cake with silky chocolate frosting—the birthday cake everyone wants.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and flour two 9-inch round pans.
Whisk flour, sugar, cocoa, baking soda, baking powder, and salt.
Add eggs, buttermilk, oil, and vanilla. Beat 2 minutes.
Stir in hot coffee (batter will be thin).
Divide between pans. Bake 30-35 minutes until toothpick comes out clean.
Cool in pans 10 minutes, then turn out onto racks.
For frosting: Beat butter until fluffy. Add cocoa and beat.
Alternately add powdered sugar and cream, beating until spreadable. Add vanilla.
Frost cooled cake layers.
recipes.story: The coffee in the batter is the secret—it doesn't taste like coffee but deepens the chocolate flavor dramatically. This is the chocolate cake against which all others are measured.
